text:
ashley: ran the mixed-tenant soak for 48h, reproduces the tail spikes we saw last week. root cause looks like eviction granularity + coalesce window alignment. short writeup below, curious about interface tradeoffs before I open an RFC.

kevin: thanks. can you sketch the failure mode?

ashley: tl;dr: long-running low-qps tenants keep small alive KV slices; when a bursty tenant hits, the batcher compacts across slices and ends up evicting the wrong in-flight sets, causing head-of-line delays.

sam: is this the same as the "lease collision" pattern we saw in the canary?

ashley: similar surface, different trigger. lease collisions were about heartbeat timing. this is about coarse eviction buckets + coalesce windows that treat multiple queues as one packing target.

jyoti: can you paste the compacting log snippet?

ashley: ```
[2026-03-12T02:11:03Z] compact-coalesce: picked window=20ms, target=256 tokens
[2026-03-12T02:11:03Z] evict: bucket=3, affected=5 tenants, evicted_inflight=2
[2026-03-12T02:11:03Z] stall: tenant=payment-svc, wait=120ms (kvcache miss)
```

lia: ugh. so eviction decisions are at bucket granularity and ignore per-tenant deadlines?

ashley: exactly. we currently only carry per-request 'priority' and token_estimate. no deadline hint. eviction picks least-recently-used at the bucket-level which looks good for throughput but bad for latency SLOs.

kevin: two obvious options: 1) finer-grained eviction (per-tenant or per-enqueue-id) 2) enrich admission API with deadline hints for soft-preempt. both have costs.

sam: finer-grained eviction increases metadata churn and GC in the queue. worried about tail overhead.

jyoti: deadline hints let runtime prefer not to evict near-deadline items. but how do we avoid mis-spec by callers? malicious or buggy callers setting high priority. need caps and quotas.

scheduler-bot: auto-note: experiment 2026-03-12 02:00 -> 2026-03-14 02:00, metric: p99-latency, delta=+48ms for mixed workload.

ashley: propose a hybrid: add optional enqueue_hint: "deadline_ms" and "eviction_group" (string). runtime uses deadline_ms to bias eviction and eviction_group to keep tight-affinity coalescing. defaults preserve current behavior.

kevin: eviction_group seems useful for tenant isolation. how would it affect packing efficiency?

ashley: we can keep packing across groups with a penalty budget. e.g., allow cross-group packing up to X tokens per window when it increases machine fill > 20%. otherwise prefer same-group packs. simple heuristic first.

sam: need telemetry — measure fill delta, p99 by group, and eviction churn. also expose a safety circuit that falls back to coarse buckets if metadata micromanagement hits CPU limit.

jyoti: concerning API surface: make enqueue_hint optional and validated server-side. documented quotas: max-deadline-distance, per-tenant eviction_group cardinality. don't expose raw priority numbers.

lia: we should also consider a runtime-only optimization: track per-group inflight-count and reserve a headroom slot per group to avoid full eviction when a burst arrives. cheap and force-isolation without changing API.

kevin: good call. shorter-term: runtime headroom + telemetry. medium-term: enqueue_hint with server-side validation + gradual rollout. long-term: rework coalesce windows to be group-aware.

ashley: I'll draft RFC with: 1) experiment logs + replay script 2) telemetry plan 3) headroom patch (opt-in flag) 4) enqueue_hint API shape + validation rules 5) perf safety circuit. any other blockers?

sam: add an integration test for attacker-sim: tenant spikes with fake-long-deadline to verify caps.

jyoti: add a docs snippet showing recommended deadline semantics for SDKs.

kevin: +1. timeline?

ashley: aiming for RFC next Tue, canary changes in 2 sprints. will tag infra and devex for SDK/telemetry work.

lia: thanks. also, let's include a short note about cost tradeoffs — more metadata = more CPU, might increase per-token cost slightly, so include sample unit-econ model in RFC.

ashley: will do. tagging @kevin @sam @jyoti for visibility :thumbsup:
